conviction_note: The four findings roughly net to zero (+2.0 on an easy Q3 lemon-price comp versus a flat-H2 consensus, +1.5 on newly-cleared Colorado River water optionality, -1.5 on an arithmetically unreachable high end to the carton guide, -2.0 on the debt-service covenant that resumes measurement at 31 Oct 2026); I tilt the net to -2.5 for the setup rather than the fundamentals - a +5.98% five-session and +7.65% twenty-session run-up to within 4.3% of the 52-week high with zero company news since 26 Aug, into the seasonally-strongest quarter of a name that fell after five of its last seven prints, is a sell-the-news configuration, and the repo's own free control (-run_up_20d) points the same way.

findings.finding: Q3 FY26 laps the second-weakest lemon price in eight quarters ($17.02/carton in Q3 FY25) while management said on 9 June that realised pricing was already above $20/carton and rising about $1/carton a month, yet the 3-analyst FY26 revenue consensus of $132.13M against $42.1M of actual H1 revenue implies H2 of ~$90.0M versus H2 FY25's $90.3M - i.e. the sell side is modelling H2 flat and giving no credit to either the price comp or the Sunkist volume shift into H2.
findings.why_not_priced: It requires stitching four separate documents - the Q1 and Q2 FY26 8-K exhibits for H1 revenue and carton prices, the FY25 10-Q for Q3 FY25's $47.478M and the $17.02 carton comp, and a 3-analyst consensus that is published only as an annual number with no quarterly split anywhere. If it were priced you would see a published Q3 revenue estimate above the $47.5M year-ago figure and at least one preview note on the cadence shift; instead stockanalysis.com carries no quarter-level estimate at all and coverage is three analysts on a name turning over roughly $930k a day.
findings.independence: Independent trade data says the same about the price direction: USDA/AMS Orlando shipping-point import prices dated 9 July 2026 show Argentine 17kg Marked Fancy lemons at $30-38 across sizes, a firm market through the middle of Limoneira's May-July quarter - https://www.indexbox.io/blog/usda-ams-orlando-shipping-point-fruit-imports-prices-report-july-9-2026/ . NOTE: this finding shares the FY26 carton-guidance arithmetic with the next finding; treat the two as one source cluster.

findings.finding: The reiterated FY26 guide of 4.0-4.5M fresh lemon cartons is arithmetically stretched: H1 FY26 delivered 681,000 (Q1, $17.41) + 1,028,000 (Q2, $16.63) = 1,709,000 cartons, down ~32% year on year, so the guide requires H2 of 2,291,000-2,791,000 against H2 FY25's 1,397,000 + 821,000 = 2,218,000 - the top end would need a Q4 (Aug-Oct, the seasonal trough) of roughly 1.9M cartons versus 821,000 last year, which the company has never done.
findings.why_not_priced: The company has framed the H1 shortfall purely as 'cadence' and reiterated the same 4.0-4.5M range at both Q1 and Q2 without ever publishing the implied H2 requirement; nobody has done the subtraction in print. If the market had, the stock would not be 4.3% off its 52-week high going in and there would be a preview flagging guidance risk - instead the only visible sell-side action in the period was a price target trimmed to $18 from $19 that cited the Sunkist transition approvingly.
findings.independence: Shares the same guidance arithmetic and the same two 8-K exhibits as the finding above - it is the negative half of the same document cluster, not separate evidence. Corroborating Q1 numbers: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1342423/000134242326000011/lmnr13126erex991.htm

findings.finding: Limoneira's lender deferred the debt service coverage ratio covenant in December 2025 so that it next resumes 'measurement as of October 31, 2026' at 1.25:1.0 - six weeks after the fiscal year the company is now two-thirds through - against H1 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of minus $9.4M (Q1 -$7.7M, Q2 -$1.7M), FY25 full-year adjusted EBITDA of minus $6.452M, total debt of $94,120,000, cash of $891,000 and only $22,096,000 of remaining revolver capacity.
findings.why_not_priced: The covenant language sits in the long-term debt note of a 10-Q for a company with three covering analysts; management's public framing is 'high confidence in positive adjusted EBITDA in the third and fourth quarters', which is a far lower bar than a 1.25x annual DSCR after a minus $9.4M first half. If the market were pricing a live covenant test you would see the stock near its 52-week low rather than 4.3% from its high, and you would see put open interest - total option open interest across the front expiry is 382 contracts with a 48%-of-mid ATM spread, so there is no protection being bought at all.
findings.independence: Partially independent confirmation of the cash strain from a different document: the 17 August 2026 8-K states the $15M Windfall Farms sale is intended to 'monetize non-core real estate assets and enhance liquidity' and carries an additional ~$4.1M impairment (explicitly a Q4 FY26 charge, so not in tonight's GAAP number) - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1342423/000110465926097890/tm2623417d1_8k.htm . Note this finding leans on the same weak-H1 EBITDA figures as the guidance findings above.

findings.finding: The federal gate for Limoneira's stated FY2026 Colorado River water monetisation opened 19 days before this print: Interior issued the post-2026 Record of Decision on 21 August 2026, ordering 1.25 million acre-feet of annual Lower Basin reductions with Arizona absorbing 760,000 acre-feet - and Limoneira decided in April 2026 to cease citrus farming on its last 600 lemon acres in Yuma specifically 'to monetize Class 3 Colorado River water rights by conserving water', telling investors it expects a monetisation event in fiscal 2026 (which ends 31 October).
findings.why_not_priced: The ROD was covered exclusively by water-policy and regional outlets - KUNC, Civil Eats, azfamily, Maven's Notebook - none of which mention Limoneira, and no financial outlet has connected a Colorado River operating rule to a $270M citrus grower. The observable test: the CFO's Form 4 shows his 1 September 10b5-1 sale executed at a $13.79 weighted average, ten days after the ROD and below where the 20-day window started, so the ROD produced no LMNR price reaction; the +5.98% five-day move began afterwards and coincided with no company news.
findings.independence: Separate outlet, separate date, same event and same compensated-conservation mechanism: https://www.kunc.org/regional-news/2026-08-24/colorado-river-plan-orders-cuts-in-the-lower-basin-while-relying-on-voluntary-conservation-upstream (2026-08-24). Limoneira's own prior monetisation precedent is a distinct document: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250123018160/en/Limoneira-Monetizes-Portion-of-Its-Premium-21000-Acre-Feet-of-Water-Rights-at-%2430000-per-Acre-Foot

SC 13D/13G activity - no 13D or 13G filed on LMNR in 2025 or 2026, so the unexplained +6% five-session run-up is not a disclosed accumulator
Insider signal - the only 2026 Form 4 cadence is Gregory C. Hamm (VP/CFO) selling exactly 1,000 shares a month under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2025-12-30; mechanical, no information

A pending Harvest at Limoneira / LLCB parcel closing inside the May-July window - the JV note discloses only cumulative distributions of $25.0M since inception and $19.3M of JV cash at 30 April, with no near-term lot-sale event; Lennar's only 2026 announcement was two new home collections on 21 April, which is a builder vertical launch, not a lot takedown

A clean primary-source year-over-year California lemon f.o.b. series for May-July 2026 versus 2025 - the USDA National Shipping Point Trends archives are PDF-only and the container has no PDF text extraction, and freshplaza (the trade coverage of the same series) returns 403 to every fetch

Avocado: I could not resolve a defensible YoY realised-price delta for the May-July window. UC Davis has California-origin terminal down 37% YoY through week 19, Rabobank (27 July) describes record supply normalising prices, but early-June USDA South District 2-layer cartons were $56-59 and 12 August LA terminal 40s were $53-55 - the signals contradict and avocado is only ~$8M of a ~$135M revenue year, so I dropped it rather than guess

Any Ventura County heat or fire event in the quarter large enough to be a lemon or avocado crop issue - the 2026 heat coverage is April-dated and about bloom and Valencia regreening, not the May-July harvest
Renewal status of the 2023 Yuma Mesa fallowing agreement (581 acres, ~$1.32M a year in quarterly instalments) beyond calendar 2025 - no filing or release confirms a 2026 continuation either way
baseline_tension: It cuts against the run-up rather than agreeing with it: the baseline shows a stock up 7.65% in twenty sessions to within 4.3% of its 52-week high with no news since 26 August, while the two hardest things I found - a debt service coverage covenant that resumes measurement on 31 October against a minus $9.4M first half, and a carton guide whose high end needs a Q4 the company has never delivered - argue the run-up has outrun the balance sheet; the 25-delta skew is null and total front-expiry open interest is 382 contracts, so there is no priced direction here to agree or disagree with, and the only genuinely new information in the window (the 21 August Colorado River Record of Decision) points the other way.
